Grant the permission for this lock first.
Allows this app to turn off the screen and lock the phone. It claims no other device admin policy.
This is what powers the Secure Lock tile. It claims only the screen-lock policy — nothing else is requested.
Powers the Screen Lock tile. This service does not read the screen; it only performs the system lock action when you tap the tile.
Pick \"Quick Lock\" under Installed apps. If the toggle is greyed out, first do Settings ▸ Apps ▸ Quick Lock ▸ ⋮ ▸ Allow restricted settings.
Two lock tiles. They differ in what the phone asks for when you come back.

The same thing the power button does. The keyguard comes up in its ordinary state, so your fingerprint unlocks it.\n\nRuns through the accessibility service. That service reads nothing and adds no window — it exists only because Android requires the lock action to be called from inside one.

Locks and demands your PIN, pattern or password on the way back in — fingerprint is refused, the same state the phone is in after a reboot.\n\nThat is not a bug to work around: Device Admin\'s lockNow() sets a strong-auth flag the system controls, and no app can opt out of it. Useful when you are handing the phone to someone.
No button below Android 13 — swipe down twice, tap the pencil, drag the tile in by hand.
To uninstall, revoke Device Admin first — Android blocks uninstalling an active device admin.
